references.text: God declares that he will stretch out his hand and strike Egypt with all his wonderful deeds, the same expression used here.
The Lord strikes Egypt with judgment, fulfilling the threat to strike the land with pestilence and plagues.
God threatens to strike the people with pestilence (דֶּבֶר) and destroy them; the same Hebrew word is used.
God threatens to wipe out (כלה) the congregation in an instant, a similar theme of destruction.
Pestilence (דֶּבֶר) is mentioned as one of the curses God will send upon the disobedient, using the same word as in the original text.
Samuel warns that God may destroy the people if they turn away, echoing the theme of being wiped out from the land.
The Lord of Hosts will wield his whip against the enemy as he struck Egypt, a reference back to the plagues.
God judges with pestilence (דֶּבֶר), using the same Hebrew word for pestilence that God threatened Pharaoh with.
Paul quotes from this context regarding Pharaoh and God's power to demonstrate his strength through him.
Ezekiel 14:19 reuses language and theology from Exodus 9:15 to emphasize God's sovereign right to destroy by pestilence.
